answer: A sport I absolutely love is cricket, which is almost a national obsession in my country. These days I mostly watch it, but I played a great deal when I was younger. I got into it as a child, playing casual games in the street with the neighbourhood kids, using a taped tennis ball and a bat my father bought me from the local market. What I love about it is the wonderful blend of strategy, skill and teamwork. As a spectator, I find major matches genuinely [[thrilling]], especially when the national team is playing. I watch almost every international match Bangladesh plays, usually at home with my father, who analyses every shot as if he were the coach. The atmosphere during a big game is electric, and the whole country seems to come to a standstill. Honestly, there is a special sense of [[unity]] that cricket brings, uniting people across all backgrounds. I still join a friendly game with old friends now and then during the holidays, as it is a fun way to stay active. What makes it so [[captivating]] is its unpredictability; a match can turn completely in a single moment. Some of the most [[nail-biting]] evenings of my life have been spent in front of the television, waiting for the final ball. I think its enduring popularity here is thoroughly deserved. For me, cricket is far more than a game; it is a shared passion that connects millions of people and brings my family together in front of the screen.

followUps.q: Have you ever watched a match in a stadium?
followUps.answer: Only once, in Dhaka, when I was staying with my elder sister. The noise and the sea of red and green shirts were unforgettable, although honestly you see the action more clearly on television.

followUps.q: Do women in your family enjoy cricket too?
followUps.answer: Yes, my younger sister is just as passionate as I am, and even my mother keeps an eye on the score during big matches. Cricket really is a family affair in our [[household]].
